subject: physics
title: Energy - Application
welcome_lead: See energy on the move - from stores to transfers.
meta_desc: KS3 Physics: applying energy transfers between stores in everyday situations.
final_note: Brilliant! You now see energy flowing through every event.

concepts.def: Kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, chemical, etc.
Energy moved between stores mechanically, electrically, by heating or radiation.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred.
Useful energy out ÷ total energy in (always less than 100%).
Energy transferred when a force moves an object; W = Fd.
The rate of energy transfer (watts); P = E ÷ t.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Energy doesn't stay still - it transfers between stores.

There are 4 ways it moves:

Mechanical (a force does work), Electrical (current in wires), Heating (hot to cold), Radiation (waves like light or sound).

You eat a sandwich (chemical store) and run. Energy transfers from chemical in your body to kinetic in your legs (mechanically).

A kettle: electrical mains energy transfers to the water's thermal store via electrical and heating pathways.

A torch: chemical (battery) -> electrical -> light + thermal.

The law of conservation of energy says:

Energy is never created or destroyed - only transferred or stored.

If you start with 100 J, you finish with 100 J. Some may end up wasted as heat or sound, but it's all still there!

options: kinetic store
gravitational store
chemical store
sound store

mcqs.q: Petrol stores energy in which form?
options: thermal
kinetic
chemical
gravitational

mcqs.q: What happens to the total resistance when you add another resistor in parallel?
options: Adding a parallel resistor doubles the voltage available.
Efficiency above 100 percent is possible if the device extracts ambient energy.
Total resistance decreases — there are more paths for current to flow.
Adding any resistor always increases the total resistance.

mcqs.q: How do you see a non-luminous object like a book?
options: Your eyes send out beams of vision that hit the book and let you see it.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
Efficiency above 100 percent is possible if the device extracts ambient energy.
Light from a source reflects off the book and enters your eyes.

mcqs.q: Can a device ever be 100 percent efficient?
options: A well-designed device can be 100 percent efficient by eliminating all friction.
Efficiency above 100 percent is possible if the device extracts ambient energy.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
In practice, no — some energy is always transferred to less useful stores (e.g. heat to surroundings).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Kinetic store”?
options: Energy in hotter objects; transferred when in contact with cooler ones.
Energy in a moving object; faster and heavier objects have more.
Energy can't be made or destroyed, only transferred from store to store.
Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Thermal store”?
options: Energy in an object held high up; bigger if mass or height is bigger.
Energy in hotter objects; transferred when in contact with cooler ones.
Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.
Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.
